- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 7d mean), model often overshoots in next 30d forecast; cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior peak or 10% below true high.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67); model often fails to revert; force forecast to align with 14d moving average if sentiment <0.50.
- When sentiment is low (0.00–0.33) and supply net is negative, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for 30d horizon.
- If 30d forecast is rising steadily (slope >0.05) and sentiment is bullish, model often fails to account for upcoming supply events; reduce forecast slope by 0.02–0.05 per event.
- For 30d forecasts with high sentiment volatility (alternating 0.00/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-point moving average.
